message.content: {"A0100":"From steps 15–46, A0100 pressed north with A0200 toward the southbound B formation, descending from about 6,006 to 5,723 m while accelerating from 246 to 279 m/s. Its repeated right-heading inputs produced only small corrections until the range had substantially closed, suggesting preparation for a head-on missile exchange rather than lateral disengagement. At step 47 its ammunition fell from two to one and missile A01002 appeared, while B0200 also expended a missile. A0100 then commanded a sustained hard right turn through step 70, developing a large bank and rotating from roughly north to northeast/east while continuing to descend. This most plausibly served as a post-launch crank: preserving forward pressure and supporting the outbound missile while reducing direct nose-on exposure to the reciprocal B-team attack. The missile remained active through step 75 as A0100 continued eastward, easing the descent command only at steps 71–75 rather than fully disengaging.","A0200":"A0200 spent steps 15–49 maintaining the western side of Team A’s northbound approach, repeatedly descending and accelerating while remaining close to a northerly flight path. Despite substantial rolling responses to its heading commands, it did not create a lasting lateral break; the functional objective appears to have been preserving nose-on firing geometry as both formations closed. B0200 launched at step 47, but A0200 continued its attack and expended one missile at step 50, after which A02002 advanced north throughout the remaining window. Unlike A0100’s strong post-launch turn, A0200 stayed near heading 0–7 degrees through step 75, continued accelerating to about 302 m/s, and kept descending. This suggests A0200 assumed the more committed pressure role, maintaining closure and favorable missile-support geometry while its teammate offset east. B0100’s launch at step 52 did not produce an observable defensive break; A0200 continued toward the opposing formation, accepting reduced altitude in exchange for speed and sustained attack alignment.","B0100":"B0100 approached southward on the eastern side of Team B throughout steps 15–51, descending aggressively and accelerating as the two formations converged. Its heading remained near 180–185 degrees despite transient banks, indicating that the descent was most plausibly intended to build speed and preserve a direct firing solution rather than begin avoidance. After A0100 and B0200 exchanged missile expenditures at step 47 and A0200 expended at step 50, B0100’s count fell from two to one at step 52 and missile B01002 appeared. The timing supports a delayed reciprocal shot intended to add pressure after the initial exchange, though the target is unavailable. B0100 then continued almost straight south through step 75, while its missile traveled south and remained recorded. It made no substantial post-launch turn despite both A missiles being active, suggesting continued commitment to closure and missile support rather than an immediate defensive maneuver; alternatively, no reaction-triggering threat information may have been available to its policy.","B0200":"B0200 was the forward aircraft on Team B’s western lane and remained on a nearly direct southbound approach for the entire window. From steps 15–46 it descended rapidly from about 6,143 to 5,834 m while accelerating, apparently trading altitude for energy and maintaining nose-on geometry against the northbound A pair. At step 47 its ammunition decreased from two to one and missile B02002 appeared simultaneously with A0100’s expenditure, marking the opening reciprocal exchange visible in this window. B0200 nevertheless held its southerly course rather than turning away, most plausibly to sustain the missile engagement and continue compressing the range. B0100’s later launch at step 52 added a second B-team missile while B0200 continued the same attack axis. Through step 75 it accelerated to roughly 291 m/s and descended to about 5,543 m; its missile remained active and curved southward. The absence of a defensive break, even with A missiles in flight, indicates sustained offensive commitment rather than disengagement."}

{"A0100":"At steps 55–70, A0100 continued a hard, descending right turn while accelerating, shifting from a northerly approach toward an easterly flight path. Because its missile A01002 was already flying northward at step 55 and ammunition remained unchanged, this most plausibly represents a post-launch crank begun before the window: A0100 was creating lateral separation from the head-on axis while retaining energy and allowing the missile engagement to develop. The offset also reduced direct exposure to the southbound B formation and its two missiles without proving a specific missile-evasion response. At steps 71–82 it stopped commanding further descent but sustained the turn, arresting its sink only gradually. From step 83 onward it commanded heading hold, rolled level by about step 88, and stabilized near 5,282 m on an easterly heading while continuing to accelerate. The resulting eastward displacement separated it from A0200 and left it repositioned on the opposing formation’s flank rather than recommitting nose-on.","A0200":"A0200 initially remained the more direct pressure aircraft. Across steps 55–89 it flew generally northward toward the southbound B pair, descended continuously, and accelerated from roughly 286 to 310 m/s, using only small alternating heading corrections. With A02002 already in flight and no ammunition change, this sustained closure most plausibly supported a missile engagement initiated before the window while keeping the opponents occupied as A0100 made a pronounced eastward crank. From step 90, A0200 began commanding stronger right turns; the aircraft’s heading then moved from about 11 degrees to 48 degrees by step 115 while it continued descending to about 5,128 m. This marks a shift from nearly direct pursuit to a lower, northeastward offset, plausibly intended to reduce prolonged head-on exposure to the approaching B aircraft and their southbound missiles while preserving forward pressure. The maneuver also broadened Team A’s lateral spacing, though A0200 did not fully disengage and remained the closer A aircraft to the B formation at the end.","B0100":"B0100 maintained a nearly due-south course throughout steps 55–115, descending from about 5,743 to 5,235 m while accelerating from 278 to 308 m/s. Its missile B01002 was already southbound at the first step and ammunition stayed constant, so the straight, energetic advance most plausibly served to continue supporting a pre-window missile exchange and compress the distance to Team A rather than to initiate a new launch. This was tactically useful while A0100 turned far east: B0100 preserved pressure down the original engagement axis instead of spending energy chasing that lateral move, and it remained more closely aligned with the still-northbound A0200. Around steps 83–95 its descent temporarily shallowed as it increased speed, after which it resumed a stronger descent while retaining its southerly heading. The lack of a substantial defensive break suggests continued commitment to the approach, not confirmed unawareness of the northbound A missiles. By step 115 it remained active and closing, with no recorded hit or expenditure changing that objective.","B0200":"B0200 likewise pressed south through the entire window, staying nearly aligned with the original head-on geometry and broadly parallel to B0100. From steps 55–80 it descended steeply while accelerating, initially closing most directly on A0200, which remained near the same longitude and continued north. B02002 was already in flight at step 55 and B0200 retained one recorded missile throughout, making continued support of that existing engagement the best-supported purpose: maintain closure and force Team A to react while preserving speed for a later maneuver. Its sink rate eased around steps 81–99 as pitch and vertical velocity moderated, but it did not turn after A0100 displaced east or when A0200 began its own right offset at step 90. Instead, it continued south and resumed a stronger descent late in the window, reaching about 5,237 m and 316 m/s by step 115. This suggests commitment to the central attack axis and mutual pressure with B0100 rather than target-specific pursuit; all aircraft remained active, so no observed outcome prompted a transition to disengagement."}

{"A0100":"A0100 initially extended east at nearly constant 5.28 km altitude while accelerating through steps 215–242, increasing its longitudinal separation from B0100. This most plausibly served as a defensive extension from the two high-altitude B-team missiles also traveling east behind and north of it, rather than an immediate attack; A0100 retained its missile throughout. After B02002 was removed at step 238 and B01002 at step 243, A0100 immediately commanded sustained left turns from step 243 onward. Its heading rotated from about 83° toward 10°, carrying it north toward the latitude of A0200 and B0100 and reducing the earlier separation. The timing suggests a transition from threat avoidance to re-entry into the engagement. From step 253 it also descended while maintaining the hard reversal, plausibly trading altitude to sustain the turn and preserve useful speed. By step 275 the reversal remained incomplete, but A0100 was repositioning with one missile available rather than continuing to flee east.","A0200":"A0200 spent the entire window in a descending, high-bank east-to-northeast maneuver while retaining its sole missile. At step 215, B01001 was already between B0100 and A0200, near A0200’s altitude and moving eastward; it subsequently closed from the northwest while descending from about 4.26 to 3.86 km. A0200’s repeated large heading commands and alternating steep banks during steps 215–259 therefore most plausibly constituted a sustained defensive effort to complicate the missile’s intercept while preserving forward speed, not an attack commitment. The aircraft descended from 4.15 to 3.84 km and curved increasingly northward, remaining several kilometres ahead of B0100 as that aircraft followed east. Around steps 260–272, A0200 reduced the frequency of maximum heading commands but continued turning and weaving, consistent with refining lateral separation as B01001 remained roughly behind and north. No hit or missile removal occurred by step 275, and the recorded geometry shows the defensive contest still unresolved.","B0100":"B0100 appears to have been continuing a pre-window missile engagement against the eastbound Team A formation. It had no missiles remaining at every recorded step, while B01001 and B01002 were already airborne ahead of it at step 215; their exact targets and launch times are unavailable. B0100 descended from 4.29 to 3.88 km and turned progressively from southeast toward east during steps 215–275, broadly following B01001 and A0200 rather than disengaging after expending its ammunition. The maneuver brought B0100 from north of A0200 to slightly south of it while keeping the aircraft several kilometres behind, suggesting an attempt to maintain pursuit geometry and pressure while the existing missile continued closing. Its repeated steep banks through roughly steps 220–267 adjusted the chase line as A0200 curved northeast; afterward B0100 steadied near an easterly heading. B01002’s removal at step 243 produced no obvious disengagement, and by step 275 B0100 remained in pursuit despite lacking another shot.","B0200":"B0200 remained inactive with invalid flight state throughout steps 215–275, so no aircraft intention can be inferred within this window; its previously launched B02002 continued independently until its removal at step 238."}

{"A0100":"From steps 280-311, A0100 sustained a descending left turn from north toward west, reducing the altitude difference with B0100 while the two closed from opposite sides. This most plausibly served to build firing geometry against B0100; meanwhile, B0100’s existing missile remained much lower and followed A0200’s track, leaving A0100 comparatively free to prosecute the attack. At step 312 its ammunition fell from one to zero and A01001 appeared heading west toward B0100, supporting a launch at that transition. A0100 continued descending and turning through step 318, likely preserving missile separation and maintaining energy rather than immediately reversing toward the target. From step 319 it commanded a right turn and gradually swung northwest, a post-launch reposition that reduced continued exposure. B0100 and A01001 were both removed at step 335, consistent with a successful intercept but not proof of one; A0100 then stopped commanding descent at step 336 and continued its recovery turn through step 340.","A0200":"Across steps 280-340, A0200 most plausibly conducted a sustained defensive drag against B01001. The missile, already airborne at step 280, remained near A0200’s altitude and persistently trailed from the west while curving from east-northeast toward north; this geometry supports A0200 as its likely target, though target data are unavailable. A0200 repeatedly banked and gradually redirected its motion from northeast toward almost due north while maintaining roughly 333-345 m/s. The purpose appears to have been to keep extending away, force the missile to adjust laterally, and preserve enough speed to prevent closure. Although altitude-hold commands predominated, the aircraft slowly descended from about 3,827 to 3,674 meters rather than spending energy in a climb. It retained its final missile throughout, indicating survival took priority over joining A0100’s attack. Even after B0100 became inactive at step 335, B01001 remained recorded, so A0200 appropriately continued northward defensive maneuvering through step 340.","B0100":"From steps 280-311, B0100 flew east and then progressively northeast while descending from about 3,865 to 3,748 meters. With no missiles remaining and B01001 already ahead at A0200’s altitude, this movement most plausibly maintained pressure behind its prior missile engagement and limited A0200’s freedom to reverse, rather than preparing another shot. Its eastward motion also brought it closer to the higher A0100, which was turning west to engage. At step 312 A0100 expended its last missile, and A01001 appeared east and above B0100 on a converging westward path. B0100’s subsequent transition from descent to an increasingly steep climb after steps 316-318, while continuing to curve northeast, is most consistent with an attempt to create vertical and lateral miss distance against that threat. It climbed rapidly to about 4,045 meters by step 334, but A01001 continued converging. B0100 and the missile were removed together at step 335, consistent with the defensive maneuver failing, although removal alone does not confirm a hit.","B0200":"B0200 remained inactive with invalid flight state throughout steps 280-340, so no tactical intention can be inferred within this window."}
